title: Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop
hints: this is really 'find the next smaller-or-equal element' for every position - which earlier pattern does that resemble?
keep a stack of indices whose final price is still undetermined; when the current price is small enough to discount some of them, resolve those
walk left to right; while the stack is non-empty and prices[current] <= prices[stack top], pop that index and set its final price to prices[popped] - prices[current]
after popping everything that qualifies, push the current index onto the stack; whatever remains on the stack at the end simply keeps its original price
commonMistakes: using a strict less-than instead of less-than-or-equal when checking if the later price qualifies as a discount
discounting by the smallest later price instead of the nearest qualifying one
forgetting indices left on the stack at the end should keep their original price, not be treated as an error

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of item prices. For each item at index `i`, look for
the nearest later item at some index `j > i` whose price is less than or
equal to `prices[i]`.

**Return the list of final prices, where an item with a qualifying later item gets `prices[j]` subtracted from its price, and an item with no such later item keeps its price unchanged.**

The discount always uses the nearest qualifying later item, not the smallest one.
constraints: the discount always uses the nearest qualifying later item, not the smallest one
notes: strictly increasing prices (no discounts at all)
all equal prices (each gets discounted by the very next one)
a single item (no later item, unchanged)

sampleTestCases.explanation: 8's nearest later price <= 8 is 4 -> 8-4=4; 4's is 2 -> 4-2=2; 6's is 2 -> 6-2=4; 2 has none <= 2 later (3 is not <= 2) -> stays 2; 3 has no later item -> stays 3
prices are strictly increasing, so no later price is ever less than or equal to an earlier one - no discounts apply
10's nearest later price <= 10 is 1 -> 10-1=9; the first 1's nearest later price <= 1 is the second 1 -> 1-1=0; the second 1 has no later price <= 1 -> stays 1; 6 has no later item -> stays 6

optimal.pattern: monotonic stack of pending indices waiting for their discount

bruteForce.approach: for each index i, scan forward through every later index j until finding one with prices[j] <= prices[i], then subtract; if none found, leave unchanged
